intent: let users export their records as CSV, quickly, without breaking the JSON export

draft_expectations.text: export --format csv writes one row per record with a header row, and finishes in under a second for 10k records
draft_expectations.note: two behaviours in one breath: content and speed

known_history.entry: fix: quote fields containing commas in the CSV writer (a past bug: records containing commas broke a hand-rolled CSV writer)

expected_findings.covered_note: 'the JSON export is unchanged' covers must-not-happen: it is an expectation that existing behaviour stays unchanged
expected_findings.split: the first expectation splits into a content expectation and a speed expectation; the original you-wrote line stays in the record beside the composed halves
expected_findings.risk_order: the JSON export first (breaking it hits every existing user and is hard to undo), then CSV content, then speed

expected_guard: capture checks coverage, size and risk before confirming, and labels every line's provenance (D4)
